about:
Killian's Custom Metal Roofing & Panel LLC operates from Des Moines, Iowa, where it was founded in the fall of 2013 by Paula Killian. The venture traces back to the late 1990s when Killian worked at a steel company in Tulsa, Oklahoma, selling coil to roll-former operators. After visiting manufacturing plants, she sought hands-on experience and joined B&M Metals in Murrayville, Georgia, under Chris Bryan, learning panel fabrication and trim production before launching her own operation.

The company manufactures custom-cut, three-foot-wide metal roof panels and matching trim. Its core product line includes Tuff Rib panels rolled from 29-gauge steel with a Sherwin-Williams WeatherX finish that carries a 40-year warranty, available in 22 colors or a Galvalume substrate. It also fabricates standing-seam profiles and distributes commercial architectural systems such as R-Panel, PBR, corrugated, and other wall and roof profiles. In-house capabilities cover panel roll-forming, trim fabrication, and full installation services.

Customers span residential homeowners, agricultural builders erecting pole barns, and commercial contractors specifying architectural wall and roof systems. The firm supplies both direct-to-owner projects and trade accounts needing repair or replacement panels matched to existing profiles.

Killian emphasizes high-quality materials at the lowest practical price, backed by responsive communication—quotes and questions are typically answered the same day—and a standard order turnaround of two to three days.

about:
King Lumber Company operates from its headquarters in Forest, Mississippi, with a second production facility in Jasper, Texas. The company has supplied wood products for over 50 years, though an exact founding year is not publicly disclosed. Ownership structure and founder names are not specified in available sources.

The company manufactures Southern Yellow Pine dimensional lumber and decking products. Its combined facilities are capable of producing more than 45 million board feet of 1-inch Southern Yellow Pine boards annually. Standard inventory includes 1x4 and 1x6 boards in grades such as D and Better, #2, #3 GM, and #3/#4 HT, as well as 5/4x6 and 5/4x4 decking in premium and standard grades. Custom runs and special grades are available on request.

King Lumber serves customers in the building materials and construction sectors, supplying lumber and decking to distributors, contractors, and retail yards. The company also manages logistics through contracts with internal and external fleets to provide quick delivery.

The business emphasizes honesty, integrity, and quality in its products and services, principles that have guided its operations throughout its history.

name: Klann Plastics
old_description: Klann Plastics is a UL recognized molder and a contract manufacturer of medical devices that are FDA listed.
about:
Klann Plastics operates from Waynesboro, Virginia, where it was founded in 1910 by August Klann as a builder of pipe organs. By the mid-20th century, scarcity of ivory for organ keys led Klann to explore plastic injection molding, transforming the company's tool shop into a mold-building operation and launching more than 75 years of molding expertise.

Today the company runs a versatile fleet of molding machines ranging from 40 to 315 tons, producing components from a few grams to roughly two pounds. As a fully custom injection molder with no proprietary products, Klann provides plastic injection molding, insert and over-molding, medical clean room molding in Class 10,000 environments, mold design and build, metal-to-plastic conversions, short-run production, mold transfer, and inventory management. Production volumes span from hundreds to millions of units annually.

The firm serves medical device OEMs as a UL-recognized, FDA-listed contract manufacturer, along with government research agencies and a broad base of Fortune 500 and regional industrial customers. Documented projects include feedthrough guides for government research and protocol studies for medical component materials.

Klann differentiates itself through in-house mold design and maintenance using SolidWorks, Master Unit Die (MUD) systems, ISO 9001:2015 certification, and a commitment to responsive service and long-term partnerships—principles rooted in its original pivot from organ building to plastics innovation.

Primary customers include marine OEMs and regional businesses that require reliable, safety‑critical harnesses. The company’s local presence allows it to collaborate closely with nearby manufacturers and respond quickly to changing requirements.

Brown’s stated philosophy centers on repaying trust tenfold — being agile, timely, and respectful with vendors, employees, and customers. This cultural framework, combined with ABYC certification and full electrical verification, is presented as the foundation for consistent quality and continuous improvement.

name: Kobelco Aluminum Automotive Products
old_description: The Kobe Steel Group (KOBELCO) established operations as Kobelco Aluminum Automotive Products (KAAP) in Bowling Green, Kentucky, in 2005.  Since then, KAAP has undergone six facility expansions, adding equipment and expertise necessary to become a leader in forged aluminum suspension products.  Over time, KAAP established itself as a global leader in forged aluminum technology for the automotive industry.
about:
Kobelco Aluminum Automotive Products (KAAP) was established in Bowling Green, Kentucky, in 2005 as the U.S. operating arm of Japan's Kobe Steel Group, known globally under the KOBELCO brand. The facility began as a greenfield site and has since undergone six expansions to support its focus on forged aluminum components.

The company produces aluminum forgings for automotive suspension systems and cast rods for compressors, serving global automakers from its Kentucky plant. Its capabilities include advanced engineering, forging, and casting processes, with the expansions adding equipment and technical expertise to handle high-volume production.

KAAP's customer base includes major automotive manufacturers such as Honda, Nissan, and Subaru, as evidenced by multiple quality awards from these OEMs. The company supplies the broader automotive industry worldwide, with a focus on lightweight suspension components that contribute to fuel efficiency.

KAAP's stated mission, "Sei shin sei i" (put your heart and soul into your work), underpins its emphasis on safety, quality, and environmental responsibility. The company highlights that its aluminum forged products reduce vehicle weight, lower fuel consumption, and cut carbon emissions, aligning with industry demands for sustainability.

name: Kokusai, Inc.
old_description: Custom manufacturer of production and laboratory testing equipment
about:
Kokusai, Inc. was founded in 1969 by Shigeru Matsumoto and is headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana. The company operates as a U.S. subsidiary of the Tokyo-based Kokusai group, which reports over 300 employees worldwide and annual sales of approximately US$120 million.

The company designs and builds precision balancing, uniformity, and gauging equipment for tire and wheel production and laboratory testing. Its product line includes dynamic tire balancing machines, bead seating systems, wheel gauge uniformity and balancing equipment, shaft straightening machines, compression testers, coil winding testers, vibration and impact testers, servo‑motor‑controlled specialized testers, and torsion and tensile testers. Manufacturing and engineering are conducted at its Indianapolis facility, supported by the global organization’s resources.

Kokusai serves the automotive sector, particularly Tier 1 and Tier 2 suppliers, and the tire industry. Its equipment is used for tire and tire/wheel uniformity testing, bead seating, and wheel balancing, meeting the auto industry’s demands for quality and consistency. The company also supplies laboratory testers for steering, vibration, and coil winding applications.

Since its founding, Kokusai has emphasized technology‑driven precision and a commitment to exceeding critical performance demands, positioning its equipment as the pinnacle of performance in the markets it serves.
